about: codelaw's rule catalogue, generated by scripts/rule-docs.py from the rule files. `title` states the rule as what the code does; `dont` and `do` are the first line of the example's don't and do that the other lacks (null when there is none, as for a deletion); `example` is the first language's full don't and do

rules.title: CSS Module class names can be read as styles.name
rules.fix_reason: renaming a class must update every file that reads it

style.description: `camelCase` (a name `styles.x` reaches without brackets), `kebab` (kebab-case) or `any` (no check)

fix_steps: Rename the class (and every `styles.…` that reads it) to camelCase.
Or set `[css] modules_convention = "camelCase"` if the bundler already maps the names.

rules.title: composes points at a class that exists
rules.fix_reason: which class to compose is the author's call
fix_steps: Correct the class name or the path.
Move `composes` into the rule whose selector is the one class that composes.

rules.title: A CSS Module stays local
rules.fix_reason: a global selector exists to reach markup outside the module, which is the author's call
fix_steps: Move the rule into a plain `.css` file, or give the markup a local class.

rules.title: A CSS Module class that is read exists
rules.fix_reason: whether to add the class or fix the name is the author's call
fix_steps: Correct the name in the JavaScript or TypeScript file, or add the class to the module.
If the bundler maps names (`localsConvention`), set `[css] modules_convention` so the mapped names count.

rules.title: A CSS Module class is read somewhere
rules.fix_reason: a class can be read by a name built at run time or by code outside the repo, so deleting its rule needs a person to accept the diff
fix_steps: Search for the class: `styles.name`, a bracket access, and any `composes` that names it.
If a component builds the name at run time, read it by a plain `styles.name` somewhere, or accept that this module is dynamic.
Otherwise delete the rule (`codelaw fix --unsafe` does it when the class is the rule's only selector).

rules.title: Dependencies are on their latest version
rules.fix_reason: a new major or minor version can change behaviour; the fix moves the range to the latest version, and the code that uses the package may need changes
fix_steps: Run `codelaw fix --unsafe` to move the range to the latest version, or edit the version by hand.
Run your package manager's install (`npm install`, `uv lock`, …) so the lockfile follows.
For a major version, read the package's changelog and update the code that uses it.
If the project must stay on this version, add the package to `[deps] ignore`, with an `expires` date when the stay is temporary.

rules.title: The dependency snapshot is recent
rules.fix_reason: refreshing the snapshot reads the registries, which needs the network; the engine never uses it (L5)
fix_steps: Run `codelaw deps refresh`: it reads npm and the Python index and writes the snapshot again.
Commit `.codelaw/deps-snapshot.json`, so CI and every teammate judge by the same facts.

rules.title: CSS classes must be used somewhere
rules.fix_reason: A class can be built at run time or used by markup outside the repo, so removing its rule needs a human or agent to accept the diff.
fix_steps: Search for the class: a name built at run time (`"btn-" + kind`) counts only through its static prefix.
If markup outside the repo uses it, add the file to `[graph] keep` or list it in the package's `style` or `exports`.
Otherwise delete the rule, or the class from its selector list.

rules.title: Exported symbols must be used somewhere
rules.fix_reason: Static analysis can't rule out reflective or external use, so removal needs a human or agent to accept the diff.
rules.dont: export function parseDate(s) { return new Date(s); }
fix_steps: Run `codelaw graph why-unused <symbol>` (`<file>#<export>` or `<module>:<name>`) to see each entry, keep and import clause.
If something outside the repo uses it, add the file to `[graph] entry` or `[graph] keep`, add its decorator to `[graph] registrars`, or tag it `/** @public */` / `# codelaw: keep`.
Otherwise delete the declaration (and its `__all__` or `export { … }` entry), or drop `export` if its own file still uses it.

Otherwise put the text in the content, where everyone can read it, and remove the attribute.

rules.title: Attributes are used only where they take effect

Use `autocomplete="new-password"` on a sign-up or change-password form.

rules.title: <button> says what type it is

rules.title: End tags have no attributes

Add its end tag there, or remove an end tag that closes nothing.

rules.title: The doctype is the HTML5 one
rules.fix_reason: switching to standards mode can change the page's layout

rules.title: Element names are HTML elements or valid custom elements
rules.fix_reason: renaming an element changes its CSS and script hooks
fix_steps: If the name is a typo of an HTML element, correct it.
If it is a custom element, give it a hyphenated name and rename its definition.
If a framework needs the name, add it to the `allow` option.

rules.title: Elements contain only content HTML allows there

rules.title: Elements that may appear once do
rules.fix_reason: which of the duplicates to keep is the author's call
fix_steps: Merge the duplicates into one, or remove the extra one.

rules.title: Children come in the order HTML requires
rules.fix_reason: moving markup may change how it is styled
fix_steps: Move the element named in the message before the one it must precede.

rules.title: Elements have a parent HTML allows
rules.fix_reason: whether to wrap the element or change it depends on the intended structure
fix_steps: Wrap the element in the parent it needs.
Or replace it with an element that fits where it is.

rules.title: Elements are inside the ancestor they need
rules.fix_reason: whether to add the ancestor or use other elements depends on the intent
fix_steps: Wrap the elements in the ancestor the message names.
Or replace them with elements that make sense where they are.

rules.title: Elements have the attributes HTML requires
rules.fix_reason: the value can only come from the author
fix_steps: Add the attribute the message names, with the right value.

rules.title: Elements contain the children HTML requires
rules.fix_reason: the content of the missing child needs a human
fix_steps: Add the child the message names, with real content.

rules.title: Headings have text
rules.fix_reason: the heading text needs a human
fix_steps: Give the heading text, or remove it if it only made space (use CSS for that).

rules.title: <title> has text
rules.fix_reason: the page title needs a human
fix_steps: Write a short title that says what the page is.

rules.title: <fieldset> has a legend
rules.fix_reason: the group's name needs a human

rules.title: Form controls have unique names
rules.fix_reason: renaming a control changes what the server receives

allowCheckboxDefault.description: allow a hidden input before a checkbox of the same name

shared.description: control types that may share a name

rules.title: Forms have a submit button
rules.fix_reason: the button's label and placement need a human
fix_steps: Add a `<button type="submit">` with a label that says what it does.

rules.title: Headings start at <h1> and go down one level at a time
rules.fix_reason: changing a heading level changes its style and the outline

minInitialRank.description: the lowest level the first heading may have (`h1`–`h6`, or `any`)

sectioningRoots.description: selectors of elements that start their own outline

rules.title: Focusable elements are not aria-hidden
rules.fix_reason: whether to unhide it, take it out of the tab order or remove it depends on the design

Otherwise take it out of the tab order with `tabindex="-1"`, or hide it from everyone with `hidden` or `inert`.

rules.title: has alt text
rules.fix_reason: only a human can describe the image, or decide it is decorative

alias.description: other attributes that count as alt text, such as a framework binding

If the image is decorative, write `alt=""`.

rules.title: Decorative images have no title
rules.fix_reason: whether the image is decorative or informative is the author's call
fix_steps: If the image carries information, move the text from `title` to `alt`.
If it is decorative, remove the `title`.

rules.title: Input attributes fit the input type
rules.fix_reason: scripts or attribute selectors may still read the attribute

rules.title: Image buttons have alt text
rules.fix_reason: the text needs a human

rules.title: Form controls have a label
rules.fix_reason: the label text needs a human
fix_steps: Add a `<label for>` with text, or wrap the control in a `<label>`.

rules.title: Links have text
rules.fix_reason: the link text needs a human
fix_steps: Give the link text, an image with `alt`, or an `aria-label`.

rules.title: Page titles are short
rules.fix_reason: shortening a title needs a human

maxlength.description: the longest title allowed, in characters

rules.title: A page stays under a line limit
rules.fix_reason: splitting a page into partials or components changes its structure

max.description: the most lines a page or template may have

skip_embedded.description: lines inside `<script>` and `<style>` do not count (the JS and CSS rules check their content)

rules.title: Special characters are escaped
aria-label doesn't repeat the label
A wrapping label has no for

rules.title: No dangerouslySetInnerHTML together with children
rules.fix_reason: which content the element should have needs the author
fix_steps: Keep either the HTML or the children, not both.

rules.title: No deprecated React APIs
rules.fix_reason: each deprecated API has its own replacement
fix_steps: Replace `ReactDOM.render` with `createRoot(el).render(…)` and `hydrate` with `hydrateRoot`.
Rename legacy lifecycles to their `UNSAFE_` names, or move their work to `componentDidMount`/`componentDidUpdate`.
Use the `prop-types` package instead of `React.PropTypes`.

rules.title: No assigning to this.state outside the constructor
rules.fix_reason: the update has to be rewritten as a `setState` call
fix_steps: Replace the assignment with `this.setState(…)`; use the updater form when the new state depends on the old.

rules.title: No findDOMNode
rules.fix_reason: a ref has to be attached to the right element by hand
fix_steps: Attach a ref to the element you need (`ref={this.ref}`).
Read `ref.current` instead of calling `findDOMNode`.

rules.title: No this.isMounted()
rules.fix_reason: the callback has to be cancelled where it starts
fix_steps: Cancel pending work in `componentWillUnmount`.
Remove the `isMounted` check.

rules.title: Components are not defined inside other components
rules.fix_reason: moving the component out means passing in the values it closed over as props
fix_steps: Move the component to the top level of the module.
Pass the values it read from the outer component as props.

rules.title: A ref's current value is not read or written during render
rules.fix_reason: moving the access into an effect or an event handler changes when it runs
fix_steps: Move the read or write into an effect, an event handler or another callback.
If the value is shown on screen, keep it in state instead of a ref.
If the ref is created lazily, initialise it inside `if (ref.current === null) { … }`.

rules.title: The return value of ReactDOM.render is not used
rules.fix_reason: code that used the instance needs a ref instead
fix_steps: Pass a ref to the root element and use it instead of the return value.

rules.title: An effect doesn't set state synchronously
rules.fix_reason: whether to derive the value, lift the state or subscribe is a design choice
fix_steps: If the value can be computed from props or state, compute it during render and drop the state and the effect.
If it depends on a change of a prop, handle the event that changed the prop instead.
If it comes from an outside source, subscribe in the effect and set the state in the subscription's callback, or use `useSyncExternalStore`.

rules.title: State is not set on every render
rules.fix_reason: what the state should be instead — derived during render, or set in an event — is a design choice
fix_steps: If the value can be computed from props or other state, compute it during render instead of storing it.
If the state must follow a prop, set it only when the prop changes: keep the previous prop in state and compare, inside an `if`.
Otherwise set it where the change happens: an event handler, or an effect's subscription callback.

rules.title: No string refs
rules.fix_reason: the ref object has to be created where the component can reach it
fix_steps: Create a ref with `useRef` or `createRef`.
Pass it as `ref={…}` and read `.current`.

rules.title: No unescaped >, ", ' or } in JSX text
rules.fix_reason: the right escape depends on the character and the author's style
fix_steps: Use an HTML entity (`'`, `"`, `>`) or a string expression (`{"'"}`).

rules.title: DOM elements use React's prop names, not HTML attribute names
A use… function calls a hook
rules.fix_reason: renaming the function means renaming every caller, in other files too
fix_steps: Rename the function without the `use` prefix (`useFormat` → `format`), and rename its callers.
If it is meant to become a hook, leave a comment naming the hook it will call.

rules.title: useState's initial value is not computed on every render
rules.fix_reason: wrapping changes behaviour when the value is itself a function, and moves the call's side effects to the first render only

rules.title: A component's props type is named <Component>Props
rules.fix_reason: renaming a type other files import would break them, so it is offered, not applied

rules.title: Render doesn't call Math.random(), Date.now() or other impure functions
rules.fix_reason: where the value should come from instead — state, an effect, an event — depends on what it is for
fix_steps: For a value made once, compute it in a `useState` initializer: `useState(() => Date.now())`.
For an id, use `useId()`.
For a value that should change, set it in an effect or an event handler.

rules.title: A class component's render() returns
rules.fix_reason: what to render needs the author
fix_steps: Return the element, or `null` to render nothing, on every path.

rules.title: Hooks are called at the top level of components and hooks
rules.fix_reason: moving a hook can change what the code does on the renders that skipped it
fix_steps: Move the hook call to the top level of the component or hook, before any early return.
Put the condition inside the hook (e.g. inside the effect) instead of around it.

rules.title: useMemo's callback computes and returns a value
rules.fix_reason: whether the code belongs in useEffect, useCallback or plain render code is the author's call
fix_steps: For a side effect, use `useEffect` instead.
For an async value, load it in an effect (or a data library) and keep it in state.
Read the values the callback needs from the component's scope instead of parameters, and return the result.

rules.title: A reducer builds its state, not the action's payload
rules.fix_reason: the reducer has to name the fields it takes from the payload
fix_steps: Copy the fields the state owns from the payload by name: `state.name = action.payload.name`.
If replacing the whole state is the point (a cache reset), write that as its own case with a descriptive action name, and suppress the finding there.

rules.title: State is plain JavaScript, not Immutable.js
rules.fix_reason: every read and update of the state is rewritten for plain objects
fix_steps: Store the state as plain objects and arrays (`fromJS(x).toJS()` once, at the boundary).
Rewrite the reducers with `createSlice`, and the reads (`state.get('a')`) as property access.

rules.title: The store is made with configureStore
rules.fix_reason: `configureStore` takes its options in another shape, and the middleware and enhancers move
fix_steps: Import `configureStore` from `@reduxjs/toolkit`.

Replace `createStore(rootReducer, preloadedState, enhancer)` with `configureStore({ reducer: rootReducer, preloadedState })`; pass extra middleware through `middleware: (getDefault) => getDefault().concat(…)`.

rules.title: A hand-written reducer doesn't change its state in place
rules.fix_reason: the update has to be rewritten to return a new value
fix_steps: Return a new value: `[...state, item]`, `{ ...state, field: value }`, `state.filter(…)`.
Better, rewrite the reducer with `createSlice`, where the in-place update is correct.

rules.title: State holds only serializable values
rules.fix_reason: the data has to be stored in another shape, and the code reading it changed
fix_steps: Store a `Map` or `Set` as an object keyed by ID, or as an array.
Store a `Date` as its ISO string or its timestamp, and make the `Date` where it is displayed.
Keep functions and class instances outside the store; store an ID that finds them.

rules.title: useSelector selects one value per call
rules.fix_reason: the one call is split into one per value, and the destructuring goes
rules.dont: const { todos, filter } = useSelector((state) => ({ todos: state.todos, filter: state.filter }));
fix_steps: Call `useSelector` once per value: `const todos = useSelector((state) => state.todos)`.
Or pass `shallowEqual` as the second argument when one object is really wanted.

rules.title: One event is one action, not a run of dispatches
rules.fix_reason: the actions have to be merged into one that the reducers all respond to

max.description: how many `dispatch` statements in a row are accepted

fix_steps: Dispatch one action that describes what happened (`orderPlaced`), with what the reducers need in its payload.
Let each slice that cares respond to it in `extraReducers`.

rules.title: A reducer has no side effects
rules.fix_reason: the side effect has to move to a thunk, a listener or a `prepare` callback
fix_steps: Make random IDs and timestamps in the action's `prepare` callback, so they arrive in the payload.
Move fetching, timers and storage into a thunk (`createAsyncThunk`) or a listener.

rules.title: connect's mapDispatch is an object of action creators
rules.fix_reason: each wrapped dispatch call is replaced by the action creator it calls
fix_steps: Replace the function with an object of the action creators it wraps: `{ todoAdded }`.
Remove the function.

example.do:
import { connect } from 'react-redux';

export default connect(mapState, { todoAdded })(TodoList);

rules.title: Reducers are written with createSlice
rules.fix_reason: the reducer, its action types and its action creators are rewritten together
fix_steps: Move the initial state and each `case` into `createSlice({ name, initialState, reducers })`, one case reducer per action.
Export the generated action creators (`slice.actions`) and the reducer (`slice.reducer`), and replace the hand-written action types and creators with them.

rules.title: Components read the store with hooks, not connect
rules.fix_reason: the component's props and its wrapper are rewritten as hook calls
fix_steps: In the component, call `useSelector` for each value `mapState` gave it, and `useDispatch` for the actions `mapDispatch` gave it.
Remove the `connect(…)` wrapper and export the component itself.

rules.title: State slices are named after their data
rules.fix_reason: the key is the state's shape, so every selector that reads it changes too
rules.do: const rootReducer = combineReducers({ users: usersReducer, posts: postsReducer });
fix_steps: Rename the key after the data: `users: usersReducer`.
Update every selector and test that reads the old key.

example.do: const rootReducer = combineReducers({ users: usersReducer, posts: postsReducer });

rules.title: `@extend` targets a placeholder
rules.fix_reason: turning a class into a placeholder changes the stylesheet's output
fix_steps: Move the shared declarations into a `%placeholder`.
`@extend` the placeholder from each place that needs it.

rules.title: No comparing to `null` in `@if`
Mixin names are kebab-case
rules.fix_reason: renaming must update every `@include` of the mixin

pattern.description: a regular expression a mixin name must match

fix_steps: Rename the mixin to match the pattern.
Rename every `@include` of it.

rules.title: No unknown at-rules (SCSS)
rules.fix_reason: the intended at-rule is the author's call

ignoreAtRules.description: at-rules to accept, such as a framework's; `/regex/` for a pattern

fix_steps: Correct the at-rule name.
If a build tool handles it, add it to `ignoreAtRules`.

rules.title: `$variables` are kebab-case
rules.fix_reason: renaming must update every use of the variable

pattern.description: a regular expression the name, without its `$`, must match

fix_steps: Rename the variable to match the pattern.
Rename every use of it.

rules.title: No empty `//` comments
No unknown functions (SCSS)
rules.fix_reason: the intended function is the author's call

ignoreFunctions.description: functions to accept; `/regex/` for a pattern

fix_steps: Correct the function name.
If it comes from a library, call it through its module (`lib.name()`), or add it to `ignoreFunctions`.

rules.title: No leading underscore in a loaded partial
Limit nesting depth
rules.fix_reason: flattening a selector is the author's call
fix_steps: Lift the inner rule out and give it its own class.
Use `&-suffix` (BEM-style names) instead of a new level.

rules.title: No duplicate `$variables`
rules.fix_reason: which declaration wins is the author's call
fix_steps: Delete the declaration that should not win.
Rename one of them if both are meant.

rules.title: No duplicate mixins
rules.fix_reason: which definition should stay is the author's call
fix_steps: Delete or rename one of the definitions.

rules.title: No global function names
No `@import`
rules.fix_reason: `@use` namespaces what it loads and loads it once, so a bare swap can change what resolves
fix_steps: Replace `@import "file"` with `@use "file"`; the members are then reached as `file.$name`, `file.mixin()`.
Use `@use "file" as *` to keep the old unprefixed names while migrating.
In an index file that only gathers other files, use `@forward`.

rules.title: No `/` as division
rules.fix_reason: `math.div` needs a `@use` of sass:math, and a slash may be CSS
fix_steps: Add `@use "sass:math";` at the top of the file.
Replace `$a / $b` with `math.div($a, $b)`.

rules.title: `%placeholder` names are kebab-case
rules.fix_reason: renaming must update every `@extend` of the placeholder

pattern.description: a regular expression a placeholder name, without its `%`, must match

fix_steps: Rename the placeholder to match the pattern.
Rename every `@extend` of it.

rules.title: AngularJS URLs use ng-href and ng-src
rules.fix_reason: the expression's value should be checked too; the rename is only the first step

rules.title: A meta Content Security Policy does not allow unsafe script
rules.fix_reason: the page's scripts have to be given nonces or hashes, or moved to files
fix_steps: Move inline script into files, or give it a nonce or a hash (`'nonce-…'`, `'sha256-…'`).
Remove `'unsafe-eval'` and replace `eval`, `new Function` and string timers.
List the origins scripts load from instead of `*` or `data:`.

rules.title: A POST form carries a CSRF token
rules.fix_reason: which token the server checks depends on its framework

names.description: extra names (field names or template tags) that count as a CSRF token, besides csrf, xsrf, authenticity_token, antiforgery, csrfmiddlewaretoken, __requestverificationtoken and _token

rules.do: <form method="post" action="/transfer"><input type="hidden" name="csrf_token" value="{{ csrf_token }}"><input name="to"></form>
fix_steps: Add the framework's field: `{% csrf_token %}` (Django), `@csrf` (Laravel), `<%= csrf_meta_tags %>` / `authenticity_token` (Rails), `{{ form.hidden_tag() }}` (Flask-WTF), or a hidden `_csrf` input.
If the form posts to another site, ignore it with `exceptions`.

example.do: <form method="post" action="/transfer"><input type="hidden" name="csrf_token" value="{{ csrf_token }}"><input name="to"></form>

rules.title: A cross-origin iframe is not given a powerful feature
rules.fix_reason: which framed sites deserve the permission is the owner's decision
fix_steps: Drop the feature from `allow`.
Or limit it to the origin that needs it: `allow="camera https://meet.example.com"`, and keep `'none'` for the rest.

rules.title: An iframe is sandboxed
rules.fix_reason: the framed page may need `allow-*` tokens, which only its author knows

rules.title: No username and password in a URL
rules.fix_reason: where the credential should live is the author's decision
fix_steps: Remove the credentials from the URL.
Send them in an `Authorization` header, or keep the request on the server.

rules.title: <base> stays on this origin
rules.fix_reason: which origin the page may use is a decision for its owner
fix_steps: Delete the `<base>` and write the URLs you need in full.
Or make its `href` a path on this origin, such as `/app/`.

rules.title: No inline event handlers
rules.fix_reason: the handler's code has to move into a script that attaches it
fix_steps: Give the element an id or a class.
Attach the listener with `addEventListener` in a script file.
Delete the `on…` attribute.

rules.title: No javascript: URLs
rules.fix_reason: the script has to move out of the URL into a listener or a real link
fix_steps: Replace a `javascript:` link with a `<button type="button">` and attach the listener with `addEventListener`.
Point `href`, `src`, `action` or `formaction` at a real URL.

rules.title: Subresources and forms load over HTTPS
rules.fix_reason: the host may not serve HTTPS; check that it does before switching

rules.title: No <object>, <embed> or <applet>
rules.fix_reason: what replaces the plugin depends on what it showed
fix_steps: Use ``, `
Use a sandboxed `<iframe>` for another document.
Use `<a download>` for a file to fetch.

rules.title: No secret in a hidden input
rules.fix_reason: where the secret should live is a design decision
fix_steps: Keep the secret on the server and send a session or a reference instead.
If the field is an anti-forgery token, name it `csrf_token`, `_csrf` or the framework's own name.

rules.title: No comment that exposes a secret or an internal host
An iframe's srcdoc holds no script
rules.fix_reason: the framed document has to become a file or be sandboxed
fix_steps: Move the document to its own file and load it with `src`.
Add `sandbox` without `allow-same-origin`.

rules.title: No template binding that writes HTML
rules.fix_reason: whether the value is trusted, and how to sanitise it, is the author's call
fix_steps: Bind text instead (`{{ value }}`, `v-text`, `x-text`, `[textContent]`).
If it must be HTML, sanitise it with a maintained library such as DOMPurify and bind the sanitised result.

rules.title: No template syntax that turns escaping off
rules.fix_reason: whether the value is trusted, and how to sanitise it, is the author's call
fix_steps: Use the escaping form: `{{ value }}` (Handlebars, Jinja, Django), `<%= value %>` (EJS).
If the value must be markup, sanitise it with a maintained library first and mark only the sanitised result safe.

rules.title: A form with a password sends it with POST over HTTPS
rules.fix_reason: a server that reads only the query string has to change with the form

rules.title: No referrer policy that leaks full URLs
rules.fix_reason: a partner may rely on the full referrer; the safer value is a suggestion

rules.title: A script or stylesheet with an integrity hash has crossorigin
rules.fix_reason: `anonymous` is right unless the file needs credentials; the suggestion assumes it does not

rules.title: No AngularJS strict contextual escaping switched off
rules.fix_reason: which sources the application loads from is a decision for the author

sanitizers.description: functions whose result may reach the sink: a callee path (global) or { name, module }; `sanitizers_mode: replace` makes them the only ones that count

fix_steps: Leave `$sceProvider.enabled` at its default (`true`).
List the hosts a template may load from in `resourceUrlWhitelist`: `["self", "https://cdn.example.com/**"]`, not `"**"`.
Pass a value to `$sce.trustAsHtml` only after a sanitizer (`$sanitize`, DOMPurify) has cleaned it.

rules.title: A cookie sets httpOnly, secure and sameSite
rules.fix_reason: a cookie a script must read, or one used cross-site, needs different flags
rules.do: res.cookie("sid", sid, { httpOnly: true, secure: true, sameSite: "lax" });

example.do: res.cookie("sid", sid, { httpOnly: true, secure: true, sameSite: "lax" });

rules.title: An Express app turns off x-powered-by or uses helmet
rules.fix_reason: `app.use(helmet())` is the better fix and needs an import; the inserted line only hides the framework

rules.title: express-session has a secret from the environment and a secure cookie
rules.fix_reason: where the secret comes from is a deployment decision
fix_steps: Read the secret from the environment or a secret store, and rotate it if it was ever committed.
Set `cookie: { secure: true, httpOnly: true, sameSite: "lax" }` in production (behind a proxy, set `trust proxy`).

rules.title: A GraphQL server limits query depth and cost, and hides introspection
rules.fix_reason: the limits that fit the schema are a decision for the author
rules.dont: const server = new ApolloServer({ typeDefs, resolvers });
fix_steps: Add a depth limit (`graphql-depth-limit`) and a cost or complexity limit to `validationRules`, and cap the page size of list fields.
Turn introspection off in production, and use persisted queries where the clients are your own.

example.dont: const server = new ApolloServer({ typeDefs, resolvers });

rules.title: helmet is not given false for a header it sets
rules.fix_reason: what the header's directives should be is a decision for the author
fix_steps: Keep the header on and tune it: give `contentSecurityPolicy` the directives the app needs.
If a header must go for one route, set it off for that route only, with a comment that says why.

rules.title: A JWT is verified with a named algorithm, never `none`
rules.fix_reason: the algorithm to name is the one the issuer signs with
fix_steps: Pass `{ algorithms: ["RS256"] }` (or the one algorithm you issue with) to `jwt.verify`.
Never put `none` in the list, and never use a public key as an HMAC secret.
Use `jwt.decode` only to read a token that `jwt.verify` has already accepted.

rules.title: A login or reset route has a rate limit
rules.fix_reason: the limits that fit the route are a decision for the author
fix_steps: Add `express-rate-limit` (or the framework's equivalent) to the route: a few attempts per minute per address and per account.
Add a lock-out or a growing delay after repeated failures, and log them.

rules.title: No archive entry name written to disk unchecked
rules.fix_reason: what to do with an entry that leaves the folder (skip, stop, report) is a decision for the author
fix_steps: Resolve the entry's path against the target folder and reject the entry when the result does not start with `target + path.sep`.
Skip symbolic links and absolute entry names; set a limit on the number and total size of entries (a zip bomb).

rules.title: No regular expression that filters HTML tags
rules.fix_reason: which tags and attributes may stay is a decision for the author
fix_steps: Sanitize with a library built for it: `DOMPurify.sanitize(html)` in the browser, `sanitize-html` on the server.
To show markup as text, escape it (`<`) instead of removing it, or write it with `textContent`.

rules.title: No byte taken modulo a number that does not divide 256
rules.fix_reason: `crypto.randomInt` needs Node 14.10 or later, and a range that starts above zero needs the bounds written

rules.title: No hidden bidirectional control characters in code
rules.fix_reason: a comment is removed whole, since its hidden text cannot be told from the rest; a string or regular expression with such a character has no mechanical fix
fix_steps: Delete the character: show hidden characters in the editor (or run `git diff --word-diff-regex=.`) and remove each one.
If a string needs right-to-left text, write the characters as escapes (`\u202E`) so the source does not hide them.

example.dont:
const level = readLevel();
// check the access level ‮ ⁦ admin

rules.title: No shell command built from a value
rules.fix_reason: the program and its arguments have to be separated by hand
fix_steps: Call `execFile` or `spawn` with the program name first and the values as an array: no shell parses them.
Leave `shell` at its default (`false`); if a shell feature (a pipe, a glob) is needed, do it in the program, not in a command string.
A value that must reach a command is checked against an allow-list first.

example.dont:
const { exec } = require("child_process");
exec("convert " + name + " out.png");

rules.title: No request made over http://
rules.fix_reason: the server must answer on HTTPS before the scheme is switched, and the text of a URL cannot be rewritten by an edit primitive
fix_steps: Change `http://` to `https://` in the URL, and check the server answers on it.
Where the host has no certificate, get one (Let's Encrypt) rather than falling back to HTTP.
A URL that is only ever local (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`) may stay; those are not flagged.

rules.title: No CORS that allows every origin together with credentials
rules.fix_reason: which origins may call the API is a decision for the author
fix_steps: List the origins that may call the API: `origin: ["https://app.example.com"]`, or a function that checks a list.
Drop `credentials: true` if the API does not use cookies; then `origin: "*"` is acceptable for public data.

rules.title: No method-override before the CSRF check
rules.fix_reason: moving a middleware changes the order every route in the file runs them in

rules.title: No dangerouslySetInnerHTML from a value that is not sanitized
rules.fix_reason: whether the value needs markup at all is a decision for the author

sanitizers.description: functions whose result may reach the sink: a callee path (global) or { name, module }; `sanitizers_mode: replace` makes them the only ones that count

fix_steps: Render the value as text (`{comment.body}`) wherever it need not carry markup.
Where it must, pass it through a sanitizer first: `DOMPurify.sanitize(html)`, and keep the allowed tags narrow.
Sanitize once, at the edge, and keep the sanitized string in its own variable so the call is next to the use.

rules.title: No token or session written to document.cookie
rules.fix_reason: the cookie has to be set by the server, which is a change to the response
fix_steps: Return the credential in the response and let the server send `Set-Cookie: token=…; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax`.
Keep the cookie out of script's reach: the page calls the API and the browser attaches the cookie.

rules.title: No script or frame source taken from a value that is not a literal
rules.fix_reason: which sources the page may load is a decision for the author
fix_steps: Use a literal URL, or pick one from a table of literal URLs by a key the code controls.
If the URL must come from configuration, check its origin against an allow-list and add `integrity` (Subresource Integrity) to the element.

rules.title: No insecure Electron window setting
rules.fix_reason: the window's preload and renderer code may rely on the setting; a setting set to `true` (such as `nodeIntegration`) has no mechanical fix and is reported as manual
rules.dont: const win = new BrowserWindow({ webPreferences: { contextIsolation: false } });
rules.do: const win = new BrowserWindow({ webPreferences: { contextIsolation: true } });

example.dont: const win = new BrowserWindow({ webPreferences: { contextIsolation: false } });
example.do: const win = new BrowserWindow({ webPreferences: { contextIsolation: true } });

rules.title: No eval, new Function or string timers
rules.fix_reason: what the string stood for (a function, a table of operations, a parser) is a design choice
fix_steps: Pass a function, not a string, to `setTimeout` and `setInterval`.
Parse data with `JSON.parse`; for an expression language use a lookup table of allowed operations or a real parser instead of `eval`.
Replace `new Function(…)` with a named function that takes its inputs as parameters.

rules.title: No request data as a format string
rules.fix_reason: it changes what is printed when the value has `%` in it

rules.title: No key or IV written into the source
rules.fix_reason: where the key comes from instead is a deployment decision
fix_steps: Read the key from the environment or a key-management service, and rotate it if it was committed.
Make a new random IV for every message with `crypto.randomBytes(12)` and store it beside the ciphertext.
Give `jwt.sign` and `createHmac` a key from the environment, not a string in the code.

rules.title: No secret written into the source
rules.fix_reason: where the secret comes from instead is a deployment decision
fix_steps: Read the value from the environment or a secret store (`process.env.NAME`, AWS Secrets Manager, Vault) at start-up.
Treat the committed value as leaked: revoke it, issue a new one and, if it must be gone from history, rewrite it.
Keep test keys in a clearly fake form (`test_key_000`) so the scanner can tell them apart.

example.do:
const awsAccessKey = process.env.AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID;
const dbPassword = process.env.DB_PASSWORD;

rules.title: No response header value taken from a request
rules.fix_reason: encoding or rejecting is a choice that depends on the header
fix_steps: Encode the value for a header (`encodeURIComponent`) or check it against an allow-list before it is written.
Reject a value that contains `\r` or `\n`.

rules.title: No escaping that stops at the first match, no one-pass stripping
rules.fix_reason: it changes how many matches are replaced, and `replaceAll` needs an ES2021 runtime

rules.title: No URL checked with a substring test
rules.fix_reason: which hosts are allowed is a decision for the author
fix_steps: Parse the value: `const u = new URL(value, base)`, and compare `u.protocol` and `u.hostname` (or `u.origin`) with exact allowed values.
To allow subdomains, compare `u.hostname === "example.com" || u.hostname.endsWith(".example.com")` (with the leading dot).
A value that fails to parse is rejected.

rules.title: No Math.random for a token, a secret or a password
rules.fix_reason: the token's length and alphabet change, and anything that checks its shape has to follow; a numeric code needs `crypto.randomInt` instead

rules.title: No javascript: URL, no navigation to a URL taken from the address
rules.fix_reason: which targets a page may navigate to is a decision for the author
fix_steps: Link to a path or an `https:` URL; put script in an event handler, not in the URL.
Parse the target with `new URL(value, location.origin)` and check `protocol` and `origin` against an allow-list before navigating.

rules.title: No jQuery call that parses a built string as HTML
rules.fix_reason: whether the value is text or markup is a decision for the author

sanitizers.description: functions whose result may reach the sink: a callee path (global) or { name, module }; `sanitizers_mode: replace` makes them the only ones that count

fix_steps: Use `.text(value)` to write a value as text.
Build elements with `$("<li>").text(name)` and append them, rather than concatenating markup.
Where markup is needed, pass the value through a sanitizer (`DOMPurify.sanitize`) first.

rules.title: No LDAP filter built from a template or concatenation
rules.fix_reason: which filter classes or escape function the project uses is its own choice
rules.do: client.search(base, { filter: new EqualityFilter({ attribute: "uid", value: name }), scope: "sub" }, callback);
fix_steps: Build the filter with the library's filter objects (ldapjs `EqualityFilter`, `AndFilter`) so values are escaped.
Where a string filter is unavoidable, escape each value for the LDAP filter syntax (RFC 4515: `\\`, `*`, `(`, `)` and NUL) before it is spliced in.

example.do: client.search(base, { filter: new EqualityFilter({ attribute: "uid", value: name }), scope: "sub" }, callback);

rules.title: No model output run, written as HTML or used as SQL
rules.fix_reason: what the program may do with model output is a design decision
fix_steps: Treat model output as untrusted input: parse it as data (`JSON.parse`) and check it against a schema before use.
Write it into the page as text (`textContent`) or through a sanitizer, never as HTML.
Never run it as code or as a shell or SQL command; let the model choose among actions the program already has.

example.do:
const out = completion.choices[0].message.content;
const data = JSON.parse(out);

rules.title: No request data written to a log unchanged
rules.fix_reason: where the value goes in the log line is the author's choice
fix_steps: Log the value as a separate field of a structured log (`logger.info({ user }, "login failed")`), which the logger escapes.
Or strip line breaks first: `value.replace(/[\r\n]/g, "")`, or `JSON.stringify(value)`.

rules.title: No request body written straight into a model
rules.fix_reason: which fields a client may set is a decision for the author
rules.do: const user = await User.create({ name: req.body.name, email: req.body.email });
fix_steps: Pick the fields: `{ name: req.body.name, email: req.body.email }`, or `_.pick(req.body, ["name", "email"])`.
Validate the body with a schema that rejects unknown keys (`zod` `.strict()`, `joi` `.unknown(false)`) before it is used.
Mark fields a client may never set (`role`, `isAdmin`) as read-only in the model.

example.do: const user = await User.create({ name: req.body.name, email: req.body.email });

rules.title: No new Buffer, no noAssert
rules.fix_reason: `Buffer.from` rejects a number, so a call that passed a size needs `Buffer.alloc`

rules.title: No file path that is not a literal
rules.fix_reason: whether a computed path is safe depends on where it comes from
fix_steps: Use a literal where the file is fixed.
Where the path is computed, resolve it against a base folder and check the result stays inside it, then suppress this finding with a reason that names the check.

rules.title: No require or import of a computed module name
rules.fix_reason: which modules may be loaded is a decision for the author
fix_steps: Name the module with a literal, or pick it from a table of literals: `const plugins = { csv: () => import("./csv.js") }`.
If the name must come from configuration, check it against an allow-list before it reaches `require`.

rules.title: No request object passed straight to a query, no $where
rules.fix_reason: which fields the query may filter on is a decision for the author
rules.do: const user = await User.findOne({ email: String(req.body.email) });
fix_steps: Build the filter from named fields and coerce each to the type the field has: `{ email: String(req.body.email) }`.
Validate the body with a schema (zod, joi, ajv) before it reaches the query; reject objects where a string is expected.
Replace `$where` with ordinary operators (`$expr`, `$gt`, …); never run a string on the database.

example.do: const user = await User.findOne({ email: String(req.body.email) });

rules.title: No redirect to an address taken from a request
rules.fix_reason: which targets are allowed is a decision for the author
fix_steps: Parse the target with `new URL(value, ownOrigin)` and redirect only when `origin` is your own, sending `pathname` (and `search`) alone.
Or accept a key (`?next=home`) and look the path up in a table of allowed paths.
Reject a value that starts with `//` or `\\` or contains a scheme you do not expect.

example.do:
const next = new URL(req.query.next, "https://app.example.com");
res.redirect(next.origin === "https://app.example.com" ? next.pathname : "/");

rules.title: No file path taken from a request
rules.fix_reason: which folder the value must stay in is a decision for the author
fix_steps: Resolve the path (`path.resolve(root, value)`) and check the result starts with `root + path.sep` before it is used.
Or look the file up by an id in a table, so no part of the path comes from the request.
With `res.sendFile`, pass the `root` option and the bare name, and reject a name that contains a separator.

rules.title: No request data in a model's system prompt
rules.fix_reason: how the prompt is split between instructions and data is a design decision
rules.dont: const messages = [{ role: "system", content: `You help ${req.query.name} with billing.` }];
fix_steps: Keep the system prompt a constant. Put the user's text in a `user` message, where the model treats it as data.
Pass facts the prompt needs (a name, a plan) through a validated, length-limited field, and say in the prompt that they are data.
Check the model's output before acting on it: see `sec-js/no-llm-output-to-sink`.

example.dont: const messages = [{ role: "system", content: `You help ${req.query.name} with billing.` }];

rules.title: No request value used as a key to write or merge
rules.fix_reason: which keys a client may set is a decision for the author
fix_steps: Use a `Map` for keys a client chooses (`settings.set(key, value)`), or create the object with `Object.create(null)`.
Reject `__proto__`, `constructor` and `prototype` as keys, or check `Object.hasOwn(allowed, key)` against a list.
Use a merge that ignores those keys (lodash 4.17.21 or later, `deepmerge` with `isMergeableObject`), or `structuredClone`, instead of copying request data into a live object.

example.dont:
const { key, value } = req.body;
config[key] = value;
example.do:
const { key, value } = req.body;
settings.set(key, value);

rules.title: No password, token or secret written to a log
rules.fix_reason: which fields to keep in the log is a decision for the author
fix_steps: Leave the value out of the message, or log an id that points to it (`userId`).
Redact known fields in the logger (`pino` `redact`, `winston` format) so a new call cannot leak them.

rules.title: No password, token or secret read from the query string
rules.fix_reason: the client has to change how it sends the value
fix_steps: Send the value in the body of a `POST` request, or in an `Authorization` header.
If a link must carry a one-time token (an e-mail verification), make it single-use and short-lived, and send `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`.

rules.title: No server environment variable in a client component, no secret in a public one
rules.fix_reason: where the secret is used from decides how the code is split
fix_steps: Read secrets only in server code (a route handler, a server component, a server action) and pass the client the result.
Name a variable `NEXT_PUBLIC_` (or `VITE_`) only when every visitor may read it; rename a secret and rotate it if it was ever public.

rules.title: No SQL built from a template or concatenation
rules.fix_reason: the statement and its values have to be separated by hand, and the placeholder style depends on the driver
rules.dont: const rows = await db.query(`SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ${id}`);
rules.do: const rows = await db.query("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = $1", [id]);
fix_steps: Write the statement as a literal with placeholders (`$1`, `?` or `:name`, as the driver wants) and pass the values as the second argument.
With a query builder (knex, Sequelize, Kysely) use its bindings: `knex.raw("id = ?", [id])`, `replacements`.
A table or column name cannot be a placeholder: pick it from an allow-list in code.

example.dont: const rows = await db.query(`SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ${id}`);
example.do: const rows = await db.query("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = $1", [id]);

rules.title: No request made to an address taken from a request
rules.fix_reason: which hosts the server may call is a decision for the author
fix_steps: Parse the URL and compare `protocol` and `hostname` with an allow-list of the hosts the feature needs.
Resolve the host and refuse private, loopback and link-local addresses (or call through a proxy that does), and do not follow redirects blindly (`redirect: "error"`).
Better still, take an id from the request and look the URL up on the server.

rules.title: No template compiled from a request, no template data taken whole from a request
rules.fix_reason: which fields the template needs is a decision for the author
fix_steps: Compile templates from files or constants in the code, never from a request value.
Pass the data object field by field: `{ name: String(req.body.name) }`, not `req.body` or `req.query` whole.
Turn off an engine's code-running features (`ejs` `client`, `pug` `compileDebug`) where they are not needed.

example.dont:
const html = ejs.render(req.query.template, { user });
res.render("profile", req.body);
example.do:
const html = ejs.render(profileTemplate, { user });
res.render("profile", { name: String(req.body.name) });

rules.title: No error object or stack trace in a response
rules.fix_reason: what the client should be told is a decision for the author
fix_steps: Log the error on the server (`logger.error(err)`), and send the client a generic message and, if useful, a request id to quote.
Set `NODE_ENV=production` so Express's default error handler hides the stack.

rules.title: No switching off of certificate checks
rules.fix_reason: a connection to a host with a self-signed certificate stops working until its CA is trusted
rules.dont: const agent = new https.Agent({ rejectUnauthorized: false, keepAlive: true });
rules.do: const agent = new https.Agent({ keepAlive: true });

example.dont: const agent = new https.Agent({ rejectUnauthorized: false, keepAlive: true });
example.do: const agent = new https.Agent({ keepAlive: true });

rules.title: No token kept in localStorage or sessionStorage
rules.fix_reason: where the token lives instead is a change to the sign-in flow
fix_steps: Have the server set the token in a cookie with `HttpOnly`, `Secure` and `SameSite`, and let the browser send it.
If a script must hold a token, keep it in memory (a closure or a module variable) and refresh it from an `HttpOnly` cookie.

rules.title: No deserializer that builds objects or runs code
rules.fix_reason: a document that uses a custom tag stops loading; js-yaml 4's `load` is already safe, so the fix only makes that explicit

rules.title: No regular expression that can run for ever, no regular expression built from a request
rules.fix_reason: what the pattern should accept is a decision for the author
fix_steps: Rewrite the pattern so no two parts can match the same text: `(a+)+` is `a+`.
Escape request data before it goes into a pattern: `value.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, "\\$&")`.
Cap the length of the input, or use an engine without backtracking (`re2`).

rules.title: No HTML written from a value that is not a literal
rules.fix_reason: a value that carries markup on purpose shows its tags as text once it is written with `textContent`

sanitizers.description: functions whose result may reach the sink: a callee path (global) or { name, module }; `sanitizers_mode: replace` makes them the only ones that count

rules.title: No method chosen by a request value
rules.fix_reason: which methods are allowed is a decision for the author
fix_steps: Compare the value with each allowed name and call the function by name.
Or look it up in a table that has no prototype (`Object.create(null)`, a `Map`) after `Object.hasOwn(table, key)`.

rules.title: No privileged branch decided by a request value
rules.fix_reason: where the decision should come from is a design choice
fix_steps: Decide from server-side state: the session, a verified token, a database row.
Remove debug and bypass switches from request handling; read them from the environment at start-up instead.

rules.title: No createCipher, no DES, RC4, Blowfish or ECB
rules.fix_reason: the key, the IV and the stored format have to change together
fix_steps: Use `createCipheriv("aes-256-gcm", key, iv)` with a random 12-byte IV per message, and keep the auth tag with the ciphertext.
Derive the key from a password with `scrypt` or `pbkdf2` and a random salt, not from the password directly.
Replace DES, RC4 and Blowfish with AES, and ECB with GCM (or CBC with a MAC).

rules.title: No MD5 or SHA-1
rules.fix_reason: the digest length changes, so what stores or compares it has to change too
fix_steps: Use SHA-256 or SHA-512 (`createHash("sha256")`) for digests and `createHmac("sha256", key)` for keyed ones.
For passwords use a password hash: `scrypt`, `argon2id` or `bcrypt` (see `sec-js/password-hash-effort`).
An MD5 used only as a cache key or a non-security checksum may stay: suppress the finding with a reason that says so.

rules.title: No short RSA key, no weak elliptic curve
rules.fix_reason: keys already issued stay weak until they are replaced, and a larger key is slower to generate and use

rules.title: No window.open without noopener
rules.fix_reason: a page that does need `window.opener` (a popup that returns a result) stops getting it

rules.title: No XPath built from a template or concatenation
rules.fix_reason: how a value is bound depends on the XPath library
rules.do: const nodes = xpath.select("//user[name=$name]", doc, false, { name });
fix_steps: Pass values as XPath variables (`$name`) where the library supports them, and bind them with its variable resolver.
If it cannot, accept only values that match a strict pattern (`^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$`) before they go into the expression.

example.do: const nodes = xpath.select("//user[name=$name]", doc, false, { name });

rules.title: No XML entity expansion
rules.fix_reason: a document that relies on its own entities stops parsing the same way

rules.title: A password is stored with a slow, salted hash
rules.fix_reason: the parameters that fit the hardware are a decision for the author, and stored hashes have to be re-made
fix_steps: Prefer `argon2id` (the `argon2` package) or `bcrypt` with a cost of 12, `scrypt` with N=2^17.
With `pbkdf2` use SHA-256 with 600 000 iterations or more, and a random 16-byte salt per password.
Never store `createHash(...).update(password)`; re-hash existing passwords at the next sign-in.

rules.title: postMessage names its target, a message handler checks the sender
rules.fix_reason: the origin to name is known only to the application
fix_steps: Give `postMessage` the exact origin of the receiver as its second argument.
In the listener, compare `event.origin` with the exact origin you expect (not `includes` or `endsWith`) and return before touching `event.data`.
Check `event.source` is the window you opened or framed when more than one window can send.

rules.title: A token, hash or signature is compared in constant time
rules.fix_reason: `timingSafeEqual` throws when the two buffers differ in length, so the length has to be compared first

rules.title: multer has size limits and a file filter
rules.fix_reason: which sizes and types are allowed is a decision for the author
fix_steps: Set `limits: { fileSize, files }` to what the feature needs.
Write a `fileFilter` that accepts only the types the feature handles, and check the file's content, not its name or `mimetype` alone.
Store uploads outside the web root, under a name the server picks.

rules.title: Cookies are `Secure`, `HttpOnly` and `SameSite`
rules.fix_reason: `secure=True` stops the cookie being set over plain HTTP in development, and `HttpOnly` hides it from scripts that read it on purpose
fix_steps: Add `secure=True, httponly=True, samesite="Lax"`.
Use `samesite="Strict"` for a session cookie; `None` needs `secure=True` and a reason.
A cookie a script must read can omit `httponly`; say so in a comment.

rules.title: Django settings are safe
rules.fix_reason: the production value comes from the deployment (environment variables, a secret manager)
fix_steps: `DEBUG = os.environ.get("DJANGO_DEBUG") == "1"`.
`ALLOWED_HOSTS = ["app.example.com"]`: list the host names you serve.
`SECRET_KEY = os.environ["DJANGO_SECRET_KEY"]`, and rotate the one that was committed.
Set `SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE`, `CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE` and `SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT` to `True`; run `python manage.py check --deploy`.

rules.title: CORS does not allow every origin with credentials
rules.fix_reason: the list of trusted origins is the application's own
fix_steps: List the origins: `allow_origins=["https://app.example.com"]`.
If the API needs no cookies, set `allow_credentials=False` and keep `*`.

rules.title: Flask's debugger is off
rules.fix_reason: the setting belongs to the environment, so the debug flag has to come from configuration
fix_steps: Remove `debug=True`; turn the debugger on with `flask --debug run` while developing.
In production run a WSGI server (`gunicorn app:app`), not `app.run`.

example.dont:
from flask import Flask

app = Flask(__name__)
app.run(debug=True)
example.do:
from flask import Flask

app = Flask(__name__)
app.run()

rules.title: Flask configuration is safe
rules.fix_reason: the production values come from the deployment (environment variables, a secret manager)
fix_steps: `app.config["SECRET_KEY"] = os.environ["FLASK_SECRET_KEY"]`, and rotate the key that was committed.
Leave `WTF_CSRF_ENABLED` on; send the token with `{{ csrf_token() }}`.
Set `SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE`, `SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY` and `SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE` to safe values.

rules.title: Hugging Face downloads pin a revision
rules.fix_reason: the commit hash to pin is a choice the author makes after reviewing the model
fix_steps: Find the commit hash of the revision you reviewed on the model's page.
Pass it: `from_pretrained(name, revision="<hash>")`.
Keep the hash in one constant or setting so an upgrade is one reviewed change.

example.dont:
from transformers import AutoModel

model = AutoModel.from_pretrained("org/model")
example.do:
from transformers import AutoModel

MODEL_REVISION = "5c9e4d1"
model = AutoModel.from_pretrained("org/model", revision=MODEL_REVISION)

rules.title: Jinja2 keeps autoescape on
rules.fix_reason: turning autoescape on changes the output of templates that write HTML on purpose; those need `|safe` or `Markup`
fix_steps: Create the environment with `autoescape=True`, or `select_autoescape()`.
Never use request data as the template: pass it as a value to a template file instead.

example.dont:
from jinja2 import Environment

env = Environment(autoescape=False)
example.do:
from jinja2 import Environment

env = Environment(autoescape=True)

rules.title: `logging.config.listen` is not used
rules.fix_reason: reconfiguring a running process needs another route (a signal handler, a config reload) the author has to choose
fix_steps: Remove the call; load the configuration from a file at start-up with `logging.config.dictConfig`.
To change levels at run time use a signal handler that re-reads the file.

rules.title: Model and array files are not unpickled
rules.fix_reason: the replacement format (`safetensors`, `.npy` without pickle, Parquet) means converting the stored files
fix_steps: Save and load arrays with `np.save` / `np.load` without `allow_pickle`, and tensors with `safetensors`.
Store tables as Parquet or CSV, not pickle.
If the file must be a pickle, load only files your own pipeline wrote and check a signature first.

example.dont:
import numpy as np

arr = np.load(path, allow_pickle=True)
example.do:
import numpy as np

arr = np.load(path)

rules.title: `assert` is not an access check
rules.fix_reason: the replacement raises the right exception for the framework, which only the author knows
fix_steps: Replace it with `if not user.is_authenticated: raise PermissionDenied`.
Use your framework's decorator (`@login_required`, `Depends(...)`) where one fits.

rules.title: A server does not bind to every interface in code
rules.fix_reason: the address belongs in configuration, with a loopback default
fix_steps: Bind to `127.0.0.1` by default and take the address from an environment variable.
A container that must listen on every interface sets it in its deployment settings, not in the code.

example.do:
import os
import uvicorn

uvicorn.run(app, host=os.environ.get("HOST", "127.0.0.1"))

rules.title: Requests go over HTTPS
rules.fix_reason: the server must serve HTTPS first, and the URL change has to follow it
fix_steps: Change the URL to `https://`.
If the server cannot do HTTPS, put it behind a proxy that can, or reach it over a private tunnel.

rules.title: No `@csrf_exempt`
rules.fix_reason: an endpoint that needs to be exempt (a webhook) needs its own authentication, which only the author can choose
fix_steps: Remove `@csrf_exempt` and send the token (`{% csrf_token %}`, or the `X-CSRFToken` header).
For a webhook, authenticate the sender (a signed header) and keep the exemption on that one view with a comment saying why.

rules.title: A request value does not choose a module or attribute
rules.fix_reason: the allow-list of names is the author's
fix_steps: Map the client's value to a fixed dict of allowed handlers: `HANDLERS = {"csv": export_csv}`; `HANDLERS[name]`.
Reject a name that is not a key.

rules.title: `exec`, `eval` and `compile` of a non-literal
rules.fix_reason: the safe replacement (`ast.literal_eval`, a lookup table, a parser) depends on what the string is for
fix_steps: For a literal (a number, a list, a dict), call `ast.literal_eval`.
For a choice among behaviours, map the input to a function through a dict.
For arithmetic or expressions, use a parser built for it, not the interpreter.

rules.title: A request value is not a format string
rules.fix_reason: the template has to be a literal, which needs the format string moved out of the request
fix_steps: Make the template a literal and pass the request value as an argument: `"Hello {}".format(name)`.
For client-written templates use `string.Template(...).safe_substitute(...)`, which has no attribute access.

rules.title: No keys or IVs in the source
rules.fix_reason: where the key comes from (a key store, an environment variable) is a deployment decision
fix_steps: Generate keys with `os.urandom` or the library (`Fernet.generate_key()`) once, and store them in a secret manager or an environment variable.
Make a fresh random IV or nonce for every message (`os.urandom(12)`) and store it beside the ciphertext.

example.do:
import os
from cryptography.fernet import Fernet

f = Fernet(os.environ["FERNET_KEY"])

rules.title: No secrets in the source
rules.fix_reason: where the secret lives instead (environment, secret manager) is a decision, and the leaked one must be rotated
fix_steps: Rotate the secret: it is in version control now.
Read it at start-up: `os.environ["DB_PASSWORD"]`, or from your secret manager.
Keep local values in an untracked `.env` file.

rules.title: A request value is not a response header
rules.fix_reason: whether to reject, strip or encode the value depends on what the header is for
fix_steps: Reject a value that contains `\r` or `\n`: `if "\n" in value or "\r" in value: abort(400)`.
Or percent-encode it: `urllib.parse.quote(value)`.
Modern servers and frameworks refuse newlines in headers; do not rely on that.

example.dont:
def view(request):
    resp = make_response("ok")
    resp.headers["X-Name"] = request.args["name"]
    return resp
example.do:
def view(request):
    resp = make_response("ok")
    resp.headers["X-Name"] = quote(request.args["name"])
    return resp

rules.title: No Telnet, FTP or SNMP v1/v2
rules.fix_reason: the replacement (SSH or SFTP, FTPS, SNMPv3) needs the server to support it
fix_steps: Use SSH or SFTP (`paramiko`, `asyncssh`) instead of Telnet and FTP, or `ftplib.FTP_TLS` for FTPS.
Use SNMPv3 (`UsmUserData` with authentication and privacy) instead of a community string.

rules.title: `secrets` for tokens, not `random`
rules.fix_reason: `secrets` has different functions (`token_hex`, `choice`, `randbelow`), so the call has to be chosen, not renamed
fix_steps: Use `secrets.token_urlsafe(32)` or `secrets.token_hex(16)` for a token.
Use `secrets.choice` for a character picked from an alphabet, `secrets.randbelow(n)` for a number.

rules.title: `mkstemp` instead of `mktemp`
rules.fix_reason: `mkstemp` returns an open file descriptor and a path, not just a name, so the surrounding code changes
fix_steps: Use `with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(delete=False) as f:` and write through `f`.
Use `tempfile.mkdtemp()` or `TemporaryDirectory()` for a directory.
Never build a path under `/tmp` by hand.

rules.title: LDAP filters are not built from strings
rules.fix_reason: the escaping function belongs to the LDAP library in use
fix_steps: Escape each value: `ldap3.utils.conv.escape_filter_chars(value)` or `ldap.filter.escape_filter_chars(value)`.
Or build the filter with `ldap.filter.filter_format("(uid=%s)", [value])`.

rules.title: Model output is not run or rendered
rules.fix_reason: what to do with the output instead (parse it against a schema, pick from a fixed list of actions) is a design choice
fix_steps: Ask the model for structured output and validate it against a schema.
Map the answer to a fixed list of actions the program already has; never pass it to a sink as text.
Escape it before it goes into HTML; use parameters for SQL.

example.do:
reply = client.chat.completions.create(model=m, messages=msgs)
action = reply.choices[0].message.content.strip()
if action in ACTIONS:
    ACTIONS[action]()

rules.title: A request value is not logged raw
rules.fix_reason: whether to strip, escape or reject the value depends on how the log is read
fix_steps: Pass the value through a helper that strips the line breaks, such as `clean(value)` with `text.replace("\r", "").replace("\n", " ")`; a method called on the request value itself is still seen as the request value.
Or log it as structured data (`extra={"name": value}`) and use a JSON formatter that escapes it.

rules.title: No Mako templates
rules.fix_reason: moving to another engine (or turning on `default_filters`) changes every template
fix_steps: Use Jinja2 with `autoescape=True`.
If you keep Mako, pass `default_filters=["h"]` to `Template` / `TemplateLookup`, and review each `|n`.

example.dont:
from mako.template import Template

t = Template(source)
example.do:
from jinja2 import Environment

env = Environment(autoescape=True)

rules.title: No `mark_safe` of dynamic text
rules.fix_reason: the right fix is escaping the parts (`format_html`, `escape`) or rendering through a template, not removing the call
fix_steps: Build HTML with `format_html("{}", value)`: it escapes `value` and trusts only the literal.
Or render a template with autoescape on.
Use `mark_safe` only on a literal, or on text you produced by escaping.

example.dont: from django.utils.safestring import mark_safe html = mark_safe("" + name + "")
example.do: from django.utils.html import format_html html = format_html("{}", name)

rules.title: A request is not splatted into a model
rules.fix_reason: which fields a client may set is the author's decision
fix_steps: List the allowed fields: `fields = ["title", "body"]`.
Build the model from named values: `Post.objects.create(title=data["title"], owner=request.user)`.
Mark server-only fields `read_only_fields`.

rules.title: A request is not a MongoDB query
rules.fix_reason: which fields the client may filter on, and their types, are the author's decision
fix_steps: Build the filter yourself from named fields: `{"name": str(request.json["name"])}`; `str()` stops an operator object from getting through.
Validate the body against a schema (pydantic, marshmallow) before it reaches the query.
Do not use `$where`; express the condition with query operators.

rules.title: A request value is not a redirect target
rules.fix_reason: the allowed destinations depend on the application
fix_steps: Redirect to a named route (`redirect(url_for("home"))`) and take only an id from the client.
Or check the target: Django `url_has_allowed_host_and_scheme(url, allowed_hosts={request.get_host()})`; elsewhere require a path that starts with a single `/`.

rules.title: A program is started by its full path
rules.fix_reason: the absolute path differs by system, so it has to come from configuration or `shutil.which` at start-up
fix_steps: Resolve it once at start-up: `GIT = shutil.which("git")`, and fail if it is `None`.
Or put the absolute path in configuration.

rules.title: A request value is not a file path
rules.fix_reason: the safe form (a lookup by id, a resolved path checked against a base folder) depends on the storage layout
fix_steps: Look the file up by an id the program issued, not by a name the client chose.
Or resolve the path and check it stays inside the base folder: `p = (BASE / name).resolve(); p.relative_to(BASE.resolve())`.
Flask: use `send_from_directory(BASE, secure_filename(name))`.

rules.title: A request value is not written into a system prompt
rules.fix_reason: what goes in the system role and what goes in the user role is a design decision
fix_steps: Keep the system prompt a constant.
Send the user's text as a separate `user` message, never concatenated into the system one.
Treat the model's answer as untrusted too (see `sec-py/no-llm-output-to-sink`).

rules.title: No `pycrypto`
rules.fix_reason: the replacement package changes the import path and some call signatures
fix_steps: Prefer `cryptography` (`pip install cryptography`).
`pycryptodomex` is a maintained drop-in with the package name `Cryptodome`: change `Crypto` to `Cryptodome`.
`pycryptodome` (not `x`) also installs a package named `Crypto`; if that is what you use, switch to `Cryptodome` so this rule can tell them apart.

rules.title: A request value is not written into the response as it is
rules.fix_reason: escaping the value or rendering a template are both fixes; which fits depends on the response
fix_steps: Escape it: `markupsafe.escape(value)` or Django's `django.utils.html.escape`.
Or render a template with autoescape on and pass the value in.
If the response is not HTML, set `Content-Type: text/plain` or `application/json`.

rules.title: A request value is not a regular expression
rules.fix_reason: `re.escape` turns the value into a literal search; a client that is meant to send a pattern needs a length limit and a timeout instead
fix_steps: If the value is text to look for, wrap it in `re.escape(value)`.
If the client must send a pattern, limit its length and run it with a timeout (the `regex` package's `timeout=`).

rules.title: Secrets are not logged
rules.fix_reason: whether to drop the value or mask it depends on what the log is for
fix_steps: Remove the value from the message.
Log an id or `"set"/"missing"`, or a masked form such as the last four characters.

rules.title: A shell command built from data
rules.fix_reason: dropping `shell=True` only works when the command is already a list of arguments; a string command must be split
fix_steps: Pass the command as a list: `subprocess.run(["ls", "-l", path])`.
Remove `shell=True`.
Replace `os.system(cmd)` with `subprocess.run([...], check=True)`; use `shlex.split` only for a trusted fixed string.

rules.title: Errors are not swallowed
rules.fix_reason: what to do with the error (log, retry, stop) is a decision
fix_steps: Catch the specific exceptions you expect.
Log the others with `logger.exception("…")` and let them go on or re-raise.

rules.title: SQL built from a string
rules.fix_reason: which placeholder style the driver takes, and where each value goes, depends on the driver
fix_steps: Write the statement with placeholders: `cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM t WHERE id = %s", (item_id,))`.
Pass the values as the second argument; the driver quotes them.
A table or column name cannot be a parameter: choose it from a fixed allow-list.
In Django use the ORM, `.raw(sql, params)` or `RawSQL(sql, params)`; give `.extra` parameters through `params=`.

example.dont:
def find(cursor, name):
    cursor.execute(f"SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = '{name}'")
example.do:
def find(cursor, name):
    cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = %s", (name,))

rules.title: A request value is not a URL to fetch
rules.fix_reason: which hosts are allowed is a policy only the author knows
fix_steps: Take an id or a key from the client and map it to a URL you wrote.
Or parse the URL and check the scheme is `https` and the host is on an allow-list, then connect to the address you resolved (not the name again).
Refuse private, loopback and link-local addresses.

rules.title: A stack trace is not sent to the client
rules.fix_reason: what the client sees instead (a generic message and an error id) is a product decision
fix_steps: Log it: `logger.exception("upload failed")`.
Return a generic message and an id the client can quote: `{"error": "internal error", "id": error_id}`.

rules.title: TLS certificate checks stay on
rules.fix_reason: the server may use a private CA, which needs the CA bundle passed as `verify=` rather than the check removed
fix_steps: Delete `verify=False`; if the server uses a private CA, pass its bundle: `verify="/etc/ssl/corp-ca.pem"`.
Use `ssl.create_default_context()` instead of `_create_unverified_context()`.
Never set `check_hostname = False` or `verify_mode = ssl.CERT_NONE`; set `minimum_version = ssl.TLSVersion.TLSv1_2` instead of an old `PROTOCOL_*`.

example.dont:
import requests

resp = requests.get(url, verify=False, timeout=5)

rules.title: No `trust_remote_code=True`
rules.fix_reason: using a model that needs custom code means reviewing and vendoring that code, which is the author's call
fix_steps: Remove `trust_remote_code=True`; use a model whose architecture is built into the library.
If you need the code, read it, copy it into your repository at a pinned commit, and load that instead.
At least pin `revision=` to a commit you reviewed.

rules.title: Deserialising with `pickle` and its relatives
rules.fix_reason: the replacement format (JSON, a schema, a signed payload) is a design choice
fix_steps: Use JSON (`json.loads`) or another data-only format, and validate the result against a schema.
If the bytes must be a pickle, sign them (`hmac`) and verify the signature before loading, or load only files the program itself wrote.
For model weights use `safetensors`.

rules.title: No DES, RC4, Blowfish or ECB
rules.fix_reason: the new cipher changes key size, nonce handling and the stored format
fix_steps: Use `cryptography`'s `AESGCM` or `ChaCha20Poly1305`: they encrypt and authenticate.
A new random nonce for every message; never reuse one with the same key.
Re-encrypt stored data under the new scheme.

example.dont:
from Crypto.Cipher import AES

cipher = AES.new(key, AES.MODE_ECB)

rules.title: No MD5 or SHA-1 for security
rules.fix_reason: whether the digest is used for security (use SHA-256) or only as a checksum (say so) is the author's call
fix_steps: If the digest guards integrity or identity, use `hashlib.sha256` or `hashlib.blake2b`.
If it is only a cache key or checksum, pass `usedforsecurity=False` and say so in a comment.
For passwords see `sec-py/password-hash-effort`.

rules.title: A shell wildcard after `tar`, `chown`, `chmod` or `rsync`
rules.fix_reason: the files have to be listed (`glob`) and passed after `--`, which changes the call
fix_steps: List the files in Python: `files = sorted(glob.glob("*.txt"))`.
Pass them as a list after `--`: `subprocess.run(["tar", "cf", out, "--", *files])`.

rules.title: No world-writable files
rules.fix_reason: the right mode depends on who has to write the file
fix_steps: Use `0o600` for a private file, `0o644` for one others read, `0o755` for a program.
Never set the others' write bit.

rules.title: XML is parsed with `defusedxml`
rules.fix_reason: `defusedxml` has to be installed and imported, and it refuses documents the standard parser accepts
fix_steps: Install `defusedxml` and import it: `import defusedxml.ElementTree as ET`.
Call the same function on it: `ET.fromstring(text)`.
For `minidom`, `sax` or `pulldom`, import the module of the same name from `defusedxml`; for `lxml`, build the parser with `resolve_entities=False, no_network=True`.

example.dont:
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

tree = ET.parse(path)
example.do:
import defusedxml.ElementTree as ET

tree = ET.parse(path)

rules.title: No `xmlrpc` without `defusedxml`
rules.fix_reason: the patch has to run once before any xmlrpc object exists, and where that is depends on the program's start-up
fix_steps: Add `import defusedxml.xmlrpc` and call `defusedxml.xmlrpc.monkey_patch()` once, before any `xmlrpc` object is made.
Or move the API to JSON over HTTP.

example.dont:
from xmlrpc.client import ServerProxy

proxy = ServerProxy(url)
example.do:
import requests

resp = requests.post(url, json=payload, timeout=10)

rules.title: XPath expressions are not built from strings
rules.fix_reason: the expression has to be rewritten around `$name` variables, and which parts are values is the author's call
fix_steps: Write the expression with variables: `tree.xpath("//user[@name=$name]", name=name)` (lxml).
ElementTree has no variables: select by a simple path and compare the attribute in Python.

rules.title: SSH host keys are checked
rules.fix_reason: where the known host keys come from is deployment-specific
fix_steps: Call `client.load_system_host_keys()` or `load_host_keys(path)`.
Use `client.set_missing_host_key_policy(paramiko.RejectPolicy())`.
Put the server's key in `known_hosts` ahead of time.

rules.title: Passwords are hashed with a slow function
rules.fix_reason: moving to Argon2 or bcrypt means rehashing at the next login and changing the stored format
fix_steps: Use `argon2-cffi` (`PasswordHasher().hash(password)`) or `bcrypt.hashpw(password, bcrypt.gensalt(rounds=12))`.
If you must use PBKDF2, use SHA-256 with at least 600 000 iterations (OWASP).
Rehash old entries when a user logs in.

example.do:
from argon2 import PasswordHasher

stored = PasswordHasher().hash(password)

rules.title: HTTP requests have a timeout
rules.fix_reason: the right timeout depends on the service; the suggested value is a starting point
fix_steps: Pass `timeout=` in seconds, or a `(connect, read)` tuple.
Keep the value in one setting if several calls share it.

rules.title: Archive extraction uses `filter="data"`
rules.fix_reason: `filter="data"` refuses members that carry device files or special permissions some archives need
fix_steps: Pass `filter="data"` (Python 3.12, and the 3.8–3.11 security releases).
Pass it to `shutil.unpack_archive(…, filter="data")` too.
Extract into a fresh folder, and never run as root.

example.dont:
import tarfile

with tarfile.open(path) as tar:
    tar.extractall(dest)
example.do:
import tarfile

with tarfile.open(path) as tar:
    tar.extractall(dest, filter="data")

rules.title: `torch.load` with `weights_only=True`
rules.fix_reason: `weights_only=True` refuses checkpoints that hold arbitrary objects; those need a conversion to `safetensors`
fix_steps: Add `weights_only=True`.
If the checkpoint holds more than tensors, convert it once with a trusted environment and keep it as `safetensors`.

rules.title: Uploaded files are saved under a safe name
rules.fix_reason: `secure_filename` removes characters a name may legitimately have, and returns an empty string for some names, which needs handling
fix_steps: Import `from werkzeug.utils import secure_filename`.
Use `secure_filename(file.filename)`, and refuse an empty result.
Better: store the file under a name you generate (a UUID) and keep the client's name as data.

example.dont:
from werkzeug.utils import secure_filename

file.save(os.path.join(UPLOADS, file.filename))
example.do:
from werkzeug.utils import secure_filename

file.save(os.path.join(UPLOADS, secure_filename(file.filename)))
