rules.title: `urlopen` of a value that may be `file://`
rules.fix_reason: the allowed schemes and hosts are policy
fix_steps: Parse the URL and check `scheme in ("http", "https")` before opening it.
Or use `requests`, which supports only HTTP(S), with a `timeout`.

example.dont:
from urllib.request import urlopen

data = urlopen(url).read()

rules.title: RSA and DSA keys are at least 2048 bits
rules.fix_reason: a longer key makes existing signatures and certificates incompatible and slows each operation
fix_steps: Use at least 2048 bits for RSA and DSA, 3072 for keys that must last past 2030.
Use `ec.SECP256R1()` or Ed25519 for new keys.
Re-issue certificates signed with the old key.

example.dont:
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric import rsa

key = rsa.generate_private_key(public_exponent=65537, key_size=1024)
example.do:
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric import rsa

key = rsa.generate_private_key(public_exponent=65537, key_size=2048)

rules.title: `yaml.safe_load` instead of `yaml.load`
rules.fix_reason: `safe_load` rejects the Python-specific tags (`!!python/object`) a document may rely on
fix_steps: Replace `yaml.load(stream)` with `yaml.safe_load(stream)`.
If you pass a `Loader`, pass `yaml.SafeLoader`.

rules.title: No bypassSecurityTrust call on a value that is not a literal
rules.fix_reason: whether the value needs to be trusted at all is a decision for the author
fix_steps: Bind the value (`[innerHTML]="body"`) and let Angular sanitize it: it keeps safe tags and drops scripts.
If an element must be trusted (a fixed SVG), pass a literal, or sanitize the value with a library first (`DOMPurify`) and add a comment that says why trust is needed.
Never trust a value that came from a request, a URL or a user.

rules.title: No HTML written to a native element or through Renderer2
rules.fix_reason: whether the value is text or markup is a decision for the author

sanitizers.description: functions whose result may reach the sink: a callee path (global) or { name, module }; `sanitizers_mode: replace` makes them the only ones that count

fix_steps: Bind the value in the template: `[innerText]="text"` for text, `[innerHTML]="html"` for markup that Angular sanitizes.
With `Renderer2`, use `setProperty(el, "textContent", value)` or `createText` and `appendChild`.
If markup is needed and trusted, sanitize it first (`DomSanitizer.sanitize(SecurityContext.HTML, value)`).

rules.title: NestJS CORS names its origins
rules.fix_reason: which origins may call the API is a decision for the author
fix_steps: Pass the origins that may call the API: `app.enableCors({ origin: ["https://app.example.com"] })`.
Keep `credentials: true` only with an explicit origin list.

example.do:
const app = await NestFactory.create(AppModule);
app.enableCors({ origin: ["https://app.example.com"], credentials: true });

rules.title: A NestJS controller has a guard
rules.fix_reason: which guard protects the route is a decision for the author
fix_steps: Add `@UseGuards(AuthGuard)` to the controller (or register `APP_GUARD` once for the app and mark public routes `@Public()`).
Add role checks (`@Roles("admin")` with a `RolesGuard`) where the route is not for every signed-in user.

rules.title: A NestJS sign-in controller is rate limited
rules.fix_reason: the limits that fit the route are a decision for the author
fix_steps: Install `@nestjs/throttler`, add `ThrottlerGuard` to the controller (or globally) and `@Throttle({ default: { limit: 5, ttl: 60000 } })` to the route.
Add a lock-out or a growing delay after repeated failures for one account, and log them.

rules.title: ValidationPipe has whitelist on
rules.fix_reason: a client that sends fields no DTO names starts getting them stripped, which can change what an endpoint does

rules.title: A Next.js server action validates its input
rules.fix_reason: the schema and the authorisation check are written by the author

validators.description: calls that check input, any one of which in the function counts: a callee path or { name, module }; `validators_mode: replace` makes yours the only ones that count

fix_steps: Parse the arguments with a schema (`zod`, `valibot`) at the top of the action and use the parsed value only.
Check the caller next: read the session and refuse when the user may not do this (`const session = await auth(); if (!session) throw …`).
Return a small, typed result; never return a database row whole.

rules.title: No request typed any
rules.fix_reason: the real shape of the request is known only to the author
fix_steps: Type the request: `Request<Params, ResBody, ReqBody, Query>` in Express, a DTO class in NestJS.
Validate the body at run time as well (see `sec-ts/no-unchecked-cast-of-input`): a type only describes what the code expects.

rules.title: No request schema that lets anything through
rules.fix_reason: a client that sends extra keys starts getting an error instead of having them kept; `z.any()` and class-validator's `validate` have no mechanical fix

rules.title: No $queryRawUnsafe or $executeRawUnsafe with a value that is not a literal
rules.fix_reason: a `${…}` in the template becomes a bound parameter, which a statement that used it for a table or column name cannot do; only `$queryRawUnsafe` with one template is rewritten
rules.dont: const rows = await prisma.$queryRawUnsafe(`SELECT * FROM "User" WHERE id = ${id}`);
rules.do: const rows = await prisma.$queryRaw`SELECT * FROM "User" WHERE id = ${id}`;

example.dont: const rows = await prisma.$queryRawUnsafe(`SELECT * FROM "User" WHERE id = ${id}`);
example.do: const rows = await prisma.$queryRaw`SELECT * FROM "User" WHERE id = ${id}`;

rules.title: No raw SQL fragment from a value in Drizzle, Kysely or MikroORM
rules.fix_reason: the statement and its values have to be separated by hand
rules.do: await db.execute(sql`select * from users where id = ${id}`);
fix_steps: Use the `sql` tagged template: each `${value}` becomes a parameter. `sql.raw` is for a fixed fragment you wrote, as a literal.
A table or column name that must vary is picked from an allow-list in code, then written with `sql.identifier(name)` (Drizzle) or `sql.id(name)` (Kysely).

example.do: await db.execute(sql`select * from users where id = ${id}`);

rules.title: No type error silenced on a line that holds a security sink
rules.fix_reason: what the right type is depends on the value
fix_steps: Fix the type instead: narrow the value, or convert it with a function that returns the type the sink wants.
If the sink really needs a value of another type, write a small typed helper for it and keep the cast inside the helper, with a comment that says why it is safe.

rules.title: No TypeORM query built from a template or concatenation
rules.fix_reason: the condition and its values have to be separated by hand
fix_steps: Write the condition with a named parameter (`"u.id = :id"`) and pass the values as the second argument: `.where("u.id = :id", { id })`.
For `repo.query`, use the driver's placeholders (`$1`, `?`) and an array of values.
A column or table name cannot be a parameter: take it from an allow-list in code.

rules.title: No type assertion on input that nothing has checked
rules.fix_reason: the schema that describes the input is written by the author

validators.description: calls that check input, any one of which in the function counts: a callee path or { name, module }; `validators_mode: replace` makes yours the only ones that count

fix_steps: Parse the value with a schema (`zod`, `valibot`, `ajv`) and use the parsed result, whose type is inferred from the schema.
In NestJS, take a DTO class with `class-validator` decorators and a `ValidationPipe`, not a cast.
For `JSON.parse`, check the shape of the result before it is used as `T`.

rules.title: A tRPC mutation is not public
rules.fix_reason: which procedure carries the auth middleware is named by the author
rules.dont: export const create = publicProcedure.input(schema).mutation(({ input }) => save(input));
fix_steps: Use `protectedProcedure` (one that runs the session check as middleware) for every mutation, and `.use(isAdmin)` where a role is needed.
If a mutation really is public (a contact form), leave `publicProcedure` and suppress this finding with a reason that says why, and rate-limit it.

example.dont: export const create = publicProcedure.input(schema).mutation(({ input }) => save(input));

rules.title: TypeORM does not synchronize the schema on start
rules.fix_reason: how the schema is changed instead (migrations) is a decision for the author
rules.dont: export const db = new DataSource({ type: "postgres", url, synchronize: true });
rules.do: export const db = new DataSource({ type: "postgres", url, migrations: ["dist/migrations/*.js"] });
fix_steps: Set `synchronize: false` (the default) and write migrations: `typeorm migration:generate`, then `migration:run` at deploy.
If it is only for a local database, set it from an environment variable that is never true in production.

example.dont: export const db = new DataSource({ type: "postgres", url, synchronize: true });
example.do: export const db = new DataSource({ type: "postgres", url, migrations: ["dist/migrations/*.js"] });

rules.title: No known typos in comments, docs and prose
rules.dont: // Retry until we recieve a response.
rules.do: // Retry until we receive a response.
fix_steps: Run `codelaw fix`: each typo becomes its correction.
For a word that is right where it stands (a product name, a quoted misspelling), excuse the line: `// codelaw-ignore spell/known-typo: <reason>`.

example.dont:
// Retry until we recieve a response.
throw new Error("Unexpected lenght of the header");
example.do:
// Retry until we receive a response.
throw new Error("Unexpected length of the header");

rules.title: A boolean @Prop defaults to false
rules.fix_reason: inverting the prop renames it for every user
fix_steps: Invert the prop's meaning so it defaults to `false` (e.g. `closable` → `hideClose`).
Update the component's markup users.

rules.title: No exported const enums
A component tag doesn't use a reserved prefix
rules.fix_reason: renaming a tag changes every page that uses it
fix_steps: Choose a prefix of your own and rename the tag.
Update every usage of the element.

rules.title: No calls at a module's top level
rules.fix_reason: where the call should run instead — a function, a lifecycle method — needs the author

allow.description: functions that may be called at the top level; setting it replaces the default list

fix_steps: Move the call into the function, method or lifecycle hook (`componentWillLoad`, `connectedCallback`) that needs its effect.
If the call builds a value, export a function that builds it, or keep it in an `export const`.
If the call must run at load time, add the function's name to the `allow` option.

rules.title: Stencil decorators only inside @Component classes
rules.fix_reason: whether the class should be a component needs the author
fix_steps: Make the class a `@Component`, or remove the Stencil decorators.

rules.title: Every slot a component renders has a @slot tag, and every @slot tag a slot
rules.fix_reason: the slot's description, or whether it should exist, needs the author
fix_steps: For a slot reported as rendered without a tag, add `@slot <name> - <what it holds>` (or `@slot - <what it holds>` for the default slot) to the JSDoc above `@Component`.
For a tag reported as never rendered, remove the tag, or render the `<slot>` it describes.

rules.title: No hostData()
rules.fix_reason: the attributes move into `render()` by hand
fix_steps: Render a `<Host>` element in `render()` with the attributes `hostData()` returned.
Remove `hostData()`.

rules.title: @Method() members are public
rules.fix_reason: whether the method is public API needs the author
fix_steps: Remove `private`/`protected`, or remove `@Method()` if it isn't public API.

rules.title: @Watch watches a @Prop or @State
rules.fix_reason: which member was meant needs the author
fix_steps: Correct the name to the @Prop or @State it should watch, or remove the watcher.

rules.title: A component's own methods are private
A component's own fields are private
DOM events are handled in render(), not with @Listen
rules.fix_reason: the handler moves into the rendered markup by hand
fix_steps: Attach the handler in `render()` (e.g. `onClick={…}` on `<Host>`).
Remove the `@Listen`.

rules.title: @Prop() members are readonly unless mutable
@Prop() members are public
rules.fix_reason: whether the field is public API needs the author
fix_steps: Remove `private`/`protected`, or make it a `@State()` if it is internal.

rules.title: Public members have JSDoc
rules.fix_reason: the documentation text needs the author
rules.do: /** The heading shown at the top. */
fix_steps: Write a `/** … */` comment above the member saying what it is for.

rules.title: Public members don't reuse HTML element names
rules.fix_reason: renaming a public member changes every user
fix_steps: Rename the member.
Update its users.

rules.title: mutable: true only on props the component changes
rules.fix_reason: whether the component should change the prop needs the author
fix_steps: Remove `mutable: true` and make the prop `readonly`, or assign it where the component means to.

rules.title: Component tags start with the project's prefix
rules.fix_reason: renaming a tag changes every page that uses it

prefix.description: the prefix every tag must start with

fix_steps: Rename the tag to start with the project's prefix.
Update every usage of the element.

rules.title: A query key is an array
rules.fix_reason: wrapping the key in an array changes its hash, so a key matched elsewhere in its old form stops matching
fix_steps: Wrap the key in an array: `queryKey: ['todos']`.

example.dont:
import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query';

useQuery({ queryKey: 'todos', queryFn: fetchTodos });
example.do:
import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query';

useQuery({ queryKey: ['todos'], queryFn: fetchTodos });

rules.title: A query key names every value its query function reads
rules.fix_reason: a new key entry changes which cache entry the query reads and writes

allowlist.description: `{ variables: [<name>…], types: [<type name>…] }`: values to leave out of the key, by name or by their declared type

rules.do: return useQuery({ queryKey: ['todo', id], queryFn: () => fetchTodo(id) });

rules.title: An infinite query's `queryFn` comes before its page-param callbacks
fix_steps: Move `queryFn` above `getPreviousPageParam` and `getNextPageParam`. The fix is offered only when every moved option is a function or a name, so the order nothing else runs in is kept.

rules.title: A mutation's `onMutate` comes before `onError` and `onSettled`
fix_steps: Move `onMutate` above `onError` and `onSettled`. The fix is offered only when every moved option is a function or a name.

rules.title: A `setQueryData` updater does not change the cached data in place
rules.fix_reason: the update has to be rewritten to build a new value
fix_steps: Return a new value built from the old one: `{ ...old, title }`, `[...old, item]`, `old.filter(…)`, `old.map(…)`.
For deep updates, build the copy with Immer's `produce(old, (draft) => { … })`, which is where an in-place change is correct.

rules.title: A query takes no option TanStack Query v5 removed
rules.fix_reason: each removed option is replaced by different code: an effect, `placeholderData`, `structuralSharing` or a hook argument
fix_steps: `onSuccess` / `onError` / `onSettled`: react to `data` or `error` where the query is rendered, move the work into the `queryFn`, or use the `QueryCache`'s global callbacks.
`keepPreviousData: true`: write `placeholderData: keepPreviousData`, importing `keepPreviousData` from TanStack Query, and read `isPlaceholderData` instead of `isPreviousData`.
`isDataEqual`: pass `structuralSharing: (old, next) => (equal(old, next) ? old : replaceEqualDeep(old, next))`.
`context`: pass the `QueryClient` as the hook's second argument.

rules.title: An option uses its TanStack Query v5 name
fix_steps: Rename the key. The fix is not offered when the object already has the new name too.

rules.title: No rest destructuring of a query result
rules.fix_reason: which fields the component needs is a choice only its author can make
rules.dont: const { data, ...rest } = useQuery({ queryKey: ['todos'], queryFn: fetchTodos });
rules.do: const { data, isPending } = useQuery({ queryKey: ['todos'], queryFn: fetchTodos });
fix_steps: Destructure the fields the component uses by name: `const { data, isPending } = useQuery(…)`.
Or keep the result whole (`const query = useQuery(…)`) and read `query.data` where it is used.

rules.title: A query hook's result is not a React hook dependency
rules.fix_reason: the fields to list depend on what the effect, callback or memo reads
fix_steps: Destructure the fields the hook reads: `const { mutate } = useMutation(…)`.
List those fields in the dependency array instead of the whole result.

rules.title: A suspense query takes no `enabled`, `placeholderData` or `throwOnError`
rules.fix_reason: removing `enabled` makes the query always run, and removing `placeholderData` shows the fallback during an update
fix_steps: `enabled`: render the component only when the query should run, or use `useQuery`.
`placeholderData`: wrap the update that changes the query key in `startTransition`.
`throwOnError`: throw `error` yourself when `!isFetching`, to send every error to the boundary.

rules.title: A query function returns its data
rules.fix_reason: what the query should return is the data the function fetches, which the author knows
fix_steps: Return the fetched data: `return res.json()`, or `return response.data`.
If the function only triggers work, it is a mutation: move it to `useMutation`'s `mutationFn`.

rules.title: A TanStack Query call takes one options object
rules.fix_reason: the positional arguments are moved into a new object, which changes the call's shape
fix_steps: Move the arguments into one object: `useQuery(key, fn, options)` becomes `useQuery({ queryKey: key, queryFn: fn, ...options })`. The fix is offered when the arguments' roles can be read off the call: an options object written in place, or a function written in place.

example.dont:
import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query';

useQuery(['todos'], fetchTodos, { staleTime: 5000 });
example.do:
import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query';

useQuery({ queryKey: ['todos'], queryFn: fetchTodos, staleTime: 5000 });

rules.title: The QueryClient is made once, not on every render
rules.fix_reason: the fix calls `React.useState` (or the imported `useState`), which must be in scope

rules.title: pyproject.toml dependencies are sorted by name
No key or table defined twice in TOML
rules.fix_reason: which of the two definitions was meant can't be known from the file
fix_steps: Decide which definition is right.
Delete the other one, or merge the two tables into one.

rules.title: pyproject.toml declares requires-python
rules.fix_reason: the supported Python range is a project decision; the fix inserts the `python` option, which may not be the right range

python.description: the range the fix writes into `requires-python`

rules.title: pyproject.toml matches its schema
rules.fix_reason: a value the schema rejects is wrong in a way only its author knows how to correct
fix_steps: Read the message: it names the key and the form the schema expects.
Rewrite the value in that form, or move a tool's setting under `[tool.<name>]`.
Run `codelaw check` on the file again until it is clean.

example.dont:
[project]
name = "app"
version = "1.0"
authors = "Ada Lovelace"
dependencies = { requests = ">=2" }
example.do:
[project]
name = "app"
version = "1.0"
authors = [{ name = "Ada Lovelace" }]
dependencies = ["requests>=2"]

rules.title: No @ts-ignore or @ts-nocheck; @ts-expect-error says why
rules.fix_reason: the reason the error is expected has to come from the author
rules.do: // @ts-expect-error: the fixture checks the compiler's message
fix_steps: Fix the type error if you can.
Otherwise replace the comment with `// @ts-expect-error: <why>`.

example.do:
// @ts-expect-error: the fixture checks the compiler's message
const n: number = "1";

rules.title: No Array constructor with several arguments
No two enum members share a value
rules.fix_reason: which value is right needs the author
fix_steps: Give each member its own value.

rules.title: No empty interfaces or {} types
rules.fix_reason: the right replacement — `object`, `unknown` or `Record<string, never>` — depends on intent
fix_steps: For any object, use `object`.
For any value, use `unknown`.
For an object with no keys, use `Record<string, never>`.

example.do:
type Options = Record<string, never>;
type Anything = unknown;

rules.title: No explicit any
rules.fix_reason: `unknown` may need narrowing code where the value is used

rules.title: No repeated non-null assertions
No constructors declared in interfaces, and no `new` methods in classes
rules.fix_reason: the intended constructor signature needs the author
fix_steps: In an interface, describe a constructor with `new (…): T`.
In a class, use `constructor(…)`.

rules.title: No TypeScript namespaces
rules.fix_reason: moving a namespace's members into a module changes every import
fix_steps: Move the namespace's members to a module of their own.
Export them, and import them where the namespace was used.

rules.title: No non-null assertion after an optional chain
rules.fix_reason: removing `!` widens the type to include `undefined`, which later code may not handle

rules.title: No require() calls
rules.fix_reason: an import may need the module's default or named exports chosen by hand
fix_steps: Replace the call with an `import` of the names the code uses.

rules.title: No aliasing this to a variable
rules.fix_reason: the callbacks that use the alias must become arrow functions by hand
fix_steps: Turn the callbacks that use the alias into arrow functions.
Use `this` directly and remove the alias.

rules.title: No extends any or extends unknown on a type parameter
rules.fix_reason: in a .tsx arrow function `<T>` alone parses as JSX and needs `<T,>`

rules.title: No interface that merges with a class of the same name
rules.fix_reason: whether to rename or to move the members into the class needs the author
fix_steps: Move the interface's members into the class, or rename the interface.

rules.title: No Function type
rules.fix_reason: the right signature needs the author
fix_steps: Write the function's real signature, e.g. `(event: Event) => void`.

rules.title: No expression statements that do nothing
rules.fix_reason: whether a call, an assignment or nothing was meant needs the author
fix_steps: Add the call or assignment that was meant, or remove the statement.

rules.title: Every declared name is used
rules.fix_reason: removing a declaration can drop the side effects of its initialiser
fix_steps: Check the initialiser has no side effect that matters.
Remove the declaration, or use it where it was meant to be used.
For a parameter that must stay for its position, prefix it with `_` and set `argsIgnorePattern: "^_"`.

example.dont:
import { readFile, writeFile } from "node:fs";
export const load = (path: string) => readFile(path);
example.do:
import { readFile } from "node:fs";
export const load = (path: string) => readFile(path);

rules.title: Primitive types, not wrapper object types
as const instead of repeating a literal as its type
namespace, not module, for a TypeScript namespace
No /// <reference path> directives
rules.fix_reason: the matching import needs the module path and what it provides
fix_steps: Replace the directive with an `import` of the module it pointed to.

rules.title: Names used only as types are imported with type
rules.fix_reason: a type-only import is erased, so code that relied on the module's side effects changes

example.dont:
import { Config, load } from "./config";
export const c: Config = load();
example.do:
import { type Config, load } from "./config";
export const c: Config = load();

rules.title: A YAML document starts with ---
GitHub Actions action metadata matches its schema
rules.fix_reason: a misshapen input or run step has several possible meanings; the author picks the one they intended
fix_steps: Read the message: it names the key and what the schema expects.
Add the missing key, or correct the key or the value.
Run `codelaw check` on the file again until it is clean.

example.dont:
name: Setup
description: Set the toolchain up
runs:
  using: composite
  step:
    - run: ./setup.sh
      shell: bash
example.do:
name: Setup
description: Set the toolchain up
runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - run: ./setup.sh
      shell: bash

rules.title: GitHub Actions are pinned to a commit SHA
rules.fix_reason: finding the commit a tag points to needs the network, and the engine never uses it (L5)
fix_steps: Look up the commit the tag points to, for example with `git ls-remote https://github.com/<owner>/<repo> <tag>`.
Replace the tag with the 40-character SHA and keep the tag as a comment: `uses: actions/checkout@<sha> # v4.2.2`.
Let Dependabot or Renovate update the pinned SHAs.

example.dont:
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
example.do:
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683 # v4.2.2

rules.title: GitHub Actions workflows match their schema
rules.fix_reason: a misshapen job or step has several possible meanings; the author picks the one they intended
fix_steps: Read the message: it names the key and what the schema expects, and suggests the key meant when the name is misspelt.
Correct the key or the value.
Run `codelaw check` on the file again until it is clean.

example.dont:
on: push
jobs:
  test:
    runs_on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: npm test
example.do:
on: push
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: npm test

rules.title: No yes/no/on/off as unquoted values
rules.fix_reason: quoting keeps the YAML 1.2 meaning (a string); if a boolean was meant, write `true` or `false` instead

rules.title: No numbers that YAML 1.1 and 1.2 read differently
rules.fix_reason: whether the octal or base-60 meaning or the YAML 1.2 meaning was intended needs the author
fix_steps: For an octal number, write it as `0o755`; for a decimal one, drop the leading zero.
For text such as a port mapping or a time, quote it: `"22:22"`.

rules.title: No key twice in one YAML mapping
rules.fix_reason: which of the two values was meant can't be known from the file
fix_steps: Decide which value the key should have.
Delete the other entry, or give it a key of its own.

example.dont:
service:
  image: nginx
  restart: always
  image: caddy

rules.title: Every alias refers to an anchor defined before it
rules.fix_reason: whether the anchor is missing, misspelt or defined too late needs the author
fix_steps: Find the anchor the alias meant.
Move the anchored node above the alias, fix the spelling, or add the anchor.

rules.title: No rule pack and no local rule is configured
fix_steps: Run `codelaw init` to install the rule packs for the languages in this repo, or add a rule under `.codelaw/rules/`.

rules.title: File is not valid UTF-8 and was skipped
fix_steps: Re-encode the file as UTF-8, or exclude it in `codelaw.toml`.

rules.title: File is larger than `[files] max_file_size` and was skipped
fix_steps: Exclude the file, or raise `[files] max_file_size` in `codelaw.toml`.

rules.title: File is marked generated and was skipped
fix_steps: Fix the generator instead, or set `[files] lint_generated = true`.

rules.title: A rule failed on this file
fix_steps: Report the rule and file to the rule's maintainer; the rest of the run is unaffected.

rules.title: File is not formatted
fix_steps: Run `codelaw format` (or `codelaw fix`) on the file.

rules.title: The formatter left the file as it was
fix_steps: If the file does not parse, correct the syntax error and run `codelaw format` again.
Otherwise the formatted text failed verification; add the file to `[format] exclude` and report it with the file attached.

rules.title: File changed on disk during the run, so the fix was not written
fix_steps: Run `codelaw fix` again once the file is no longer being edited.

rules.title: The fixed file could not be written, so it is unchanged
fix_steps: Make the file writable (its permissions, a read-only disk, a full disk), then run `codelaw fix` again.

rules.title: A `codelaw-ignore` comment has no reason
fix_steps: Write the reason after a colon: `codelaw-ignore <rule>: <reason>`.

rules.title: A `codelaw-ignore` comment suppresses nothing
A deprecated symbol is used
fix_steps: Replace the use with the replacement `.codelaw/deprecations.toml` names (or the deprecation marker's message gives).
An existing use may stay until its deadline only through `.codelaw/baseline/graph--no-deprecated-usage.toml`, which a person adds with `codelaw baseline add`.

rules.title: A baseline entry allows more findings than its file has
fix_steps: Run `codelaw baseline prune` (or `codelaw fix`, which prunes too) to lower the entry; lowering is always safe.

rules.title: An exception (a baseline entry, a deprecation, a `codelaw-ignore`) expires within its warning window
fix_steps: Fix the findings the exception covers before its `expires` date: on that day they are reported again and the exception is an error.
To keep it longer, a person moves `expires` later with `codelaw baseline add --expires …` (a baseline entry) or edits the comment; `codelaw baseline check` flags an extended deadline for review.

rules.title: An exception reached its `expires` date and no longer covers anything
fix_steps: Fix the findings it covered; they are reported again at their rule's own severity.
Then remove the exception: `codelaw baseline prune` (or `codelaw fix`) lowers a baseline entry, and the `codelaw-ignore` comment is deleted by hand.

rules.title: An exception has no `expires` date while `[exceptions] require_expiry` is on
fix_steps: Add `expires = "YYYY-MM-DD"` (the first day it no longer holds): `codelaw baseline add --expires …` rewrites a baseline entry; a `codelaw-ignore` takes `expires=YYYY-MM-DD` before its colon.

rules.title: An exception's `added_by` is not an email address, or not the git author of the change
fix_steps: Set `added_by` (`by=` in a `codelaw-ignore`) to your own git email, `git config user.email`; `codelaw baseline add` writes it for you.

rules.title: A `codelaw-ignore` comment names a rule that does not exist
fix_steps: Correct the rule id, or remove the comment.

rules.title: A new or edited function is reached by no test file
fix_steps: Write a unit test that imports the function (or its module, for a function the module does not export) and calls it: a test needs judgment, so codelaw does not write one.

If the function should never need its own test (a thin wrapper, generated code), exempt it in `.codelawignore` with `forever: <reason>`; to defer the test, give the line `expires=YYYY-MM-DD` and `on_touch=…` and a reason.

rules.title: A new or edited function's line coverage is under `[coverage] min`
fix_steps: Add test cases that run the lines the coverage report shows as missed, regenerate the lcov report in the same job, and run `codelaw check --coverage <report>` again: a test needs judgment, so codelaw does not write one.
If the function cannot reasonably be covered, exempt it in `.codelawignore` with a reason, `expires=` or `forever`, and `on_touch=`.

rules.title: The coverage report does not match this file, so its coverage is not judged
fix_steps: Regenerate the lcov report from the code being checked — in the same CI job, after the tests and before `codelaw check` — and pass it with `--coverage` or `[coverage] report`.

rules.title: A `.codelawignore` line matches no file or function
A `.codelawignore` line is missing a field or contradicts itself, so it exempts nothing
fix_steps: Give the line what the message names: a reason after a colon (always, with `expires=` or `forever`), `expires=YYYY-MM-DD` or `forever` (`[coverage.ignore] require_expiry`), and `on_touch=error|warn|keep` unless it is `forever` (`[coverage.ignore] require_on_touch`).
`forever` takes no `expires=`, `warn_days=` or `on_touch=`; a glob takes no `on_touch_scope=function`.
